title: Scheduler tuning: workload buckets + queue policy adjustments to protect tail latency under mixed prompt lengths
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Problem
- We are seeing p99 latency sensitivity when a pool serves a mix of short prompts (chat) and long-context prompts (RAG / long system prompts), especially at moderate-to-high concurrency.
- Current queue/scheduler behavior tends to let long-prefill requests dominate GPU time, creating head-of-line (HoL) blocking for short requests. This shows up as p99 spikes without a proportional throughput improvement.

Goal
- Introduce workload buckets and queue policy adjustments that preserve tail latency under mixed prompt lengths while retaining competitive throughput.
- Ensure behavior is deterministic and tuneable via the new hardware tuning profile pack (per-SKU defaults).

Non-goals
- Rewriting the entire scheduler or inventing a new admission control algorithm from scratch.
- Model-specific special casing beyond model-family heuristics already tracked in the profile pack.

Proposed approach
1) Workload buckets (per request / per route)
- Bucket requests based on estimated prefill cost and expected decode length.
- Initial buckets (names are internal; we can tweak):
  - S (short): small prefill, short decode (typical chat)
  - M (medium): moderate prefill and decode
  - L (long-prefill): large prefill / long context
  - XL (very long): worst-case contexts (guardrailed)
- Signals available at request time:
  - prompt_tokens (or estimated from tokenizer)
  - max_output_tokens
  - streaming=true/false (bias towards fairness for streaming)
  - model family / quant profile (optional: affects prefill/decode ratio)

2) Queue policy adjustments
- Partition internal queues by bucket with weighted fairness.
- Add per-bucket concurrency caps to prevent L/XL from starving S.
- Add “prefill/decode interleave” policy knobs:
  - ensure decode steps cannot be perpetually delayed by prefill batches
  - cap consecutive prefill cycles when S queue depth is non-zero
- Provide sane defaults per SKU in the profile pack (H100 can tolerate more concurrency; L40S needs more conservative caps).

3) Guardrails
- Explicitly protect p99 at the cost of a small throughput reduction under mixed workloads.
- Define a rollback-safe flag set so we can revert to pre-existing behavior quickly if regression is observed.

Instrumentation / observability requirements (ties to ENG-4931)
- Export scheduler_queue_ms by bucket + route + model (tag cardinality to be bounded; see observability guidance).
- Export counters:
  - scheduler_bucket_selected{bucket}
  - scheduler_starvation_prevented_total
  - scheduler_prefill_cycles_capped_total
  - scheduler_queue_depth{bucket} (sampled)

Acceptance criteria
- Benchmark-lab mixed workload scenario shows:
  - p99 latency improvement of >= 15% vs baseline for S bucket requests while L requests are present
  - no more than 5% throughput regression on “steady short chat” workload (all-S)
  - no increase in error rate or timeouts attributable to scheduler
- Perf-canary: alerts do not trigger for p95/p99 deltas outside rollout guardrails during Hosted canary.
- Behavior is controllable via profile pack knobs and reflected in startup debug log (active bucket policy + caps).

Test plan
- Unit tests: bucketing classification and precedence.
- Integration tests: synthetic mix (S + L) verifying S requests do not exceed configured queueing bound.
- Benchmark-lab matrix additions: include mixed distribution (e.g., 70% S, 25% M, 5% L) and adversarial burst (short burst while long prefill is ongoing).

Rollout plan
- Land behind feature flag: runtime.scheduler.workload_buckets.enabled
- Enable for Hosted canary cohort first (small region/model mix); observe for 48h.
- Dedicated: keep opt-in until customer comms and SLO validation are complete.

Links
- GitHub PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24895
- Perf-canary integration tracking: ENG-4930
- Profile pack selection + overrides: ENG-4923

Open questions
- Do we prefer strict per-bucket queue partitions vs a single queue with dynamic priority? (Current PR uses partitions; confirm this is consistent with profile pack knob surface.)
- How should we treat “max_output_tokens” vs observed decode length for bucketing when clients set very large max tokens? (Currently clamp to a percentile-based cap per route; confirm this is acceptable.)
- Should streaming requests always be treated as S/M to preserve UX? (Tentative: yes, but keep a cap to avoid abuse.)
comments: 2026-01-10 (Noah Patel): Creating this as the scheduler workstream for the profile pack. Primary failure mode we need to solve is HoL blocking when long-context prefill enters the queue. Let’s bias towards predictable tail latency; we can accept small throughput loss as long as it’s documented + stable.

2026-01-13 (Sofia Ivanova): Drafted bucketing heuristic using prompt_tokens + max_output_tokens. Added a conservative default: if tokenizer estimate missing, treat as M (avoid misclassifying huge prompts as S). Will send PR for review end of week.

2026-01-17 (Marcus Reed): Bench harness can generate mixed workload distributions. I’ll add two scenarios: (1) steady-state mix 70/25/5 and (2) adversarial: long-prefill every 10th request + short burst at t=30s. Need clear pass/fail gates for p99 of S bucket.

2026-01-22 (Grace Kim): Heads up: kernel v3 on H100 changes prefill/decode balance slightly; schedule fairness may need retuning for H100 vs L40S. Please ensure knobs are per-SKU via profile pack (don’t hardcode caps).

2026-01-27 (Sofia Ivanova): PR up (24895). Key changes: queue partitions by bucket; weighted round-robin with a cap on consecutive prefill cycles if S queue has backlog. Added counters for starvation prevention and bucket selection. Still need to wire scheduler_queue_ms histogram tags (blocked on metrics map finalization).

2026-02-02 (Allison Grant): Please keep metric cardinality bounded. Avoid tagging by full route string if it explodes; prefer normalized route_id or service tier. Also, bucket labels are fine. We should sample queue depth gauges to avoid high-frequency emission.

2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE POV, I need a clean rollback switch: one flag that returns us to prior scheduler behavior, plus a way to confirm active mode via /health or startup log. Also, please document what changes in expected behavior docs (p99 should improve under mix; throughput may dip).

2026-02-10 (Sofia Ivanova): Addressed rollback semantics: runtime.scheduler.workload_buckets.enabled gates all new behavior. Added startup log line showing enabled + per-bucket caps. Still working with Omar on queueing-vs-compute trace split so we can validate what actually improved.

2026-02-14 (Rina Kobayashi): Benchmark-lab run (H100) looks good: S p99 down ~18% on the mixed scenario; throughput -2% on all-S. L40S run shows larger benefit but we hit OOM at higher concurrency if L bucket not capped tightly; please make L40S defaults more conservative.

2026-02-16 (Sofia Ivanova): Updated L40S defaults in profile pack draft (lower L/XL concurrency caps; more aggressive prefill-cycle cap when S backlog > 0). Requesting review from Lena on backpressure interactions.

2026-02-18 (Lena Fischer): Reviewed interaction with admission control/backpressure. Looks OK but watch for oscillation: if we cap prefill too hard, decode backlog can grow and cause bursts. Suggest adding a small hysteresis window on ‘S backlog’ signal (e.g., require backlog for N ms before enforcing cap).
2026-02-20 (Sofia Ivanova): Added hysteresis (configurable). Marking ticket In Review pending final metrics wiring + perf-canary gating sign-off. Targeting merge by runtime-1.22 cut.
